newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to host global AIDS conference in 2000.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to host global AIDS conference in 2000.

text.p: South Africa's east coast port city of Durban has been chosen to host the largest gathering of scientists in Africa in the year 2000 for a global AIDS conference, officials said on Thursday.

Up to 15,000 people, generating some 130 million rand ($30 million), were expected to attend the 10-day meeting, the first to be held outside an industrialised centre in Europe and the Americas, said co-chairman of the South African bid committee Gustaaf Wolvaardt.

"The conference is now accessible to scientists throughout Africa, which will stimulate appropriate research. It will focus international attention to South African research, forcing us to fast-track our development programme," Wolfaardt told a news coference.
Durban was chosen ahead of Spain's Madrid and Barcelona, and Birmingham in Britain after an intense three-year bid programme co-chaired by South African Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma and Wolvaardt.

One of the reasons South Africa was chosen was its rapidly growing epidemic of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), which destroys the body's immmune system, resulting in Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), said Hoosen Coovadia who will be conference chairman.

Durban, KwaZulu-Natal province's largest city, was an ideal venue because it had South Africa's highest percentage of HIV-infected people with about 24 percent of women testing positive at ante-natal clinics, he said.
Africa also had two thirds of the world's HIV-infected people, Coovadia said.

Spain's Barcelona was chosen as the 2002 venue because it had the highest prevalence of HIV and AIDS in Europe, and it could constitute a link to Latin America, the International AIDS Society said in a statement.
Eleven of the biennial conferences have been held, with Geneva hosting the 1998 conference.
